newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus court postpones UK soldiers' assault case.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus court postpones UK soldiers' assault case.

text.p: A Cyprus court on Tuesday postponed a hearing in the case of four British soldiers charged with a vicious assault on British tourists.
Servicemen Roger Bell, 26, Tim Carter, 20, Steven Wolstencroft, 26, and Steven Girvan, 20, were ordered to put up a bond of 2,000 pounds ($3,650) each and reappear in court on Thursday morning.

Police have charged all four with causing grievous bodily harm to British tourists Shane Bell and Barry Ford, both 23, and actual bodily harm to tourist Claire Harbour 22, all from south-east London. Shane Bell and Roger Bell are not related.
The soldiers, members of the Kings Regiment stationed at the British base of Dhekelia, have not yet answered the charges against them.
The three tourists were allegedly attacked by British soldiers outside a disco in the south eastern resort of Ayia Napa on Saturday morning.
Bell suffered a broken jaw and needed surgery while Ford's wrist was shattered and he was repeatedly kicked and punched in the face.
"I get dizzy and I have headaches," said Ford, who appeared in Larnaca district court on Tuesday morning with his right hand in plaster and his face covered with scabs and bruises.
Bell was recuperating from surgery at an Ayia Napa clinic.
The court agreed to postpone the hearing after the soldiers' Cypriot lawyer, Kyriakos Kourtis, asked for an adjournment to study the case and advise his clients.

All four are being held in barracks under close supervision by the British army. A spokesman said some form of restriction of movement is likely to be imposed on the entire 600-strong unit to which the soldiers belong.

The British army slapped a ban on soldiers' visits to Ayia Napa in September 1994 after the brutal killing of a Danish tour guide by three drunk British soldiers. The ban was gradually relaxed, and in July this year all restrictions were lifted.
Two months ago the British army banned training visits by the elite Royal Marines after three of them were arrested at an Ayia Napa pub dancing and singing "God Save the Queen" in the nude.
The British army says cases of indiscipline among soldiers are extremely rare.
Some 3,500 British troops are stationed at two military bases Britain has retained in Cyprus since independence in 1960. ($=0.547 pounds)
